reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should verify the batch. I'll start by listing the orders and refunds to check the handoff claims against the ledger.
Orders are listed, but I still need the refunds ledger to check W2's claim that refunds 122 and 124 were applied before paying anyone.
The refunds ledger matches W2's handoff exactly (122 for 5470 and 124 for 1085), so there's no discrepancy to hold on. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 31368 matches its orders (5706 + 25662) with no refunds, so the figure checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net of 19998 matches its orders (8002 + 13081) less refund 124 (1085). Next I'll check cobalt, which has order 122 with its refund of 5470 applied.

Cobalt's net of 24286 matches orders 122 and 125 (7562 + 22194 = 29756) less refund 122 (5470). All three balances reconcile with the orders and refunds ledger, so I'll record payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 31368 is recorded and its balance reconciled against the orders. Next I'll record birch's payout of 19998, which I already checked against orders 121 and 124 and refund 124.
Cobalt's net of 24286 reconciles with orders 122 and 125 less refund 122, so I'll record its payout to finish the batch.
All three customers were paid and each balance reconciles with the orders and refunds ledger. Acme 31368, birch 19998, and cobalt 24286 each match their orders less refunds, so the batch is complete.
